title: Home lifting - restart and muscle emphasis plans
description: Original conservative programming for a returning recreational lifter. Generic exercise content only; personal profile and login live outside the public repo.
assumptions: Usable dumbbells or adjustable dumbbells and a stable flat bench.
No barbell rack, safety arms, machines, pull-up bar or adjustable bench is assumed.
No current limiting injury; current symptoms must be assessed before hard training.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
cues: Plant both feet and keep the bench stable.
Keep wrists stacked over forearms; lower under control.
Keep elbows roughly 30-60 degrees from the torso; use a comfortable depth.
Use only dumbbells you can position and put down safely.
exercises.regression: Use the dumbbell floor press instead; record the changed exercise ID.

exercises.name: Neutral-grip dumbbell floor press
cues: Palms face each other; keep wrists straight.
Let upper arms touch the floor softly; do not bounce.
Press smoothly; stop before repetitions become a grind.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
cues: Use a fixed surface that cannot slide or tip.
Keep head, trunk and hips in one line.
Lower the chest toward the support, then push away.
Record support height or support description every session.
exercises.regression: Use a higher fixed surface or a wall. A loose chair is not a safe support.

exercises.name: Bench-supported single-arm dumbbell row
cues: Support yourself on a stable bench; keep the trunk quiet.
Row the elbow toward the hip without twisting.
Lower smoothly and use the same range on both sides.
exercises.regression: Use a lighter dumbbell; rest between sides if needed.

exercises.name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
cues: Use very light weights and a stable hip hinge.
Keep elbows softly bent; open the arms without swinging.
Stop around torso level; keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.regression: Use no added weight. If the bent-over position hurts, omit and add no replacement sets.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
cues: Stand tall and lift the shoulders straight up.
Pause briefly, then lower; do not roll the shoulders.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold one secure dumbbell close to the chest.
Keep the whole foot planted and let knees track with toes.
Squat only as low as you can control comfortably.
exercises.regression: Unloaded squat to a stable bench or sit-to-stand; record the bodyweight variant.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Keep a soft knee bend and send the hips backward.
Keep the weights close and the spine comfortable and steady.
Stop at a hamstring stretch before your lower back rounds; floor contact is unnecessary.
Stand tall without leaning backward.
exercises.regression: Rehearse unloaded hip hinges. If uncomfortable, use a bodyweight glute bridge with its own exercise ID.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Start unloaded, with light hand support if needed.
Step back and lower smoothly through a comfortable range.
Push through the front foot to stand; keep the movement balanced.
Log left and right separately; the side is the front working leg.
exercises.regression: Use a shorter comfortable range with hand support, or substitute the goblet-squat bodyweight variant.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise on floor
cues: Use a stable support for balance.
Rise smoothly, pause, and lower slowly on the flat floor.
Begin bodyweight; later use one dumbbell and retain the same support.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Keep ribs over hips and knees relaxed.
Start with elbows slightly in front of the torso.
Press in a comfortable path without leaning backward.
exercises.regression: Use lighter weights. If overhead motion is painful, omit it and seek assessment rather than forcing the movement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Use light weights with a small elbow bend.
Raise slightly forward of your sides to about shoulder level if comfortable.
Keep thumbs neutral or slightly upward; avoid swinging.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell curl
cues: Curl both arms together; count one simultaneous repetition as one rep.
Keep the upper arms quiet and wrists comfortable.
Lower under control without leaning or swinging.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hammer curl
cues: Keep palms facing each other and curl both arms together.
Count one simultaneous repetition as one rep.
Keep elbows close to the torso; do not swing.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dumbbell triceps extension on floor
cues: Use light dumbbells and a secure grip.
Bend at the elbows with the upper arms steady.
Keep the weights away from your face and move slowly.
exercises.regression: If elbows are uncomfortable, omit this exercise; keep only the pain-free close-grip floor press already in the plan.

exercises.name: Close-grip dumbbell floor press
cues: Use a neutral grip and keep elbows comfortably close.
Lower gently until upper arms touch the floor.
Do not bang the dumbbells together or bounce the elbows.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: Lie on your back with hips and knees bent.
Exhale gently while moving opposite arm and leg.
Keep the trunk quiet and shorten the reach if your back arches.
Side means the extending leg.
exercises.regression: Move only the legs or tap one heel at a time.

exercises.name: Side plank
cues: Put the elbow under the shoulder.
Keep the trunk aligned and breathe normally.
Start with bent knees if necessary.
Side means the side supporting the body on the floor.
exercises.regression: Use bent knees and 10-15 second holds.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Keep feet planted and ribs relaxed.
Lift the hips by squeezing the glutes; do not arch the back.
Pause briefly, then lower smoothly.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

exercises.name: Easy walk
cues: Walk at a pace where you can speak in full sentences.
Use flat, safe ground; no running is required.
exercises.regression: Walk for 5-10 minutes and gradually extend the time.

exercises.name: Gentle mobility circuit
cues: Use easy shoulder circles, ankle circles and comfortable trunk rotations.
Move slowly and stay in a pain-free range.
Skip any movement that causes symptoms.
exercises.regression: Use less load and a comfortable range of motion.

steps.notes: A preparation set, not fatigue training.

steps.notes: Use a stable bench and a comfortable range.

steps.label: Unloaded hip hinge
steps.notes: Send hips back with a soft knee bend.

steps.label: Gentle ankle rocks
steps.notes: Each side, holding a stable support.

steps.label: Rehearsal / ramp-up sets
steps.notes: Before the first loaded exercise, do 1-3 easy sets of 5-10 reps, gradually approaching today's working load. Add one easy rehearsal set when changing to a new movement pattern. Log these as warm-up sets; never use an old PR to set the load.

instructions: Optional gentle stretches only if comfortable; no forceful stretching.

notes: Use the program's first-two-weeks set cap; the table shows the weeks 3-4 maximum.
Keep 3-4 good repetitions in reserve during the first four weeks.
The first week can be 25-35 minutes. Do not add sets just to fill an hour.

programs.name: Four-week restart

phases.name: Relearn the movements
phases.notes: Easy walking on other days. If this is still too much, split the first session over two days without adding volume.

phases.name: Build the habit
phases.notes: Use two sessions instead of three if soreness affects normal movement.

phases.name: Build basic capacity
phases.notes: Add the second set only when the first set and next-day recovery are comfortable; staying at one set is allowed.

phases.name: Continue full body if preferred
phases.notes: Optional indefinite continuation instead of switching to the focus program. Alternate B/A/B then A/B/A; keeping an easier earlier phase is also allowed. This does not add lifting days.

programs.transitionPolicy: Never auto-switch programs. Staying on three full-body sessions is a good long-term option. Offer the focus program after four weeks only if recovery is comfortable and there is no limiting pain or breathing symptom.

programs.name: Five focus days with two easy days

phases.name: Transition to the split
phases.notes: These are the first two weeks after selecting this program, normally overall weeks 5-6. Keep existing loads; do not increase load and volume together. If recovery worsens, return to three full-body sessions.

phases.name: Steady training
phases.notes: Normally overall week 7 onward. Add a third listed set one exercise at a time. Optional work remains opt-in and is never needed just to reach an hour.

programs.missedDayPolicy: Resume the next session in sequence; do not stack missed workouts. Keep at least one intervening non-pressing day between shoulder, arm and chest sessions if shifting the calendar.
